The Iron Five • O'Connell Siblings & Wright Twins

Five Family Members. One Unbreakable Sanctuary.

Unlike traditional rock bands assembled by label A&R departments, The Stardust Engine is a five-person family unit: siblings Ryan, Cassidy, and Holly O'Connell and their identical twin maternal cousins Evan and Tyler Wright.

📜 Read Complete Band History (1985–Present) → 🗂️ View Classic Roster Dossier →
CPI Class of 1988 • T10 Paraplegic Wheelchair User • Cassidy’s Safe Person

Ryan O'Connell

Co-Lead Vocals, Lead Electric Guitar & Lyricist

Born in Blacksburg, Virginia, Ryan co-founded the band with his sister Cassidy at Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute (CPI) in 1985. After surviving the December 1990 I-81 black-ice tour crash as a T10 paraplegic, Ryan refused to surrender the stage—performing from his custom manual wheelchair and anchoring Cassidy as her lifelong safe person.

📄 Full Archival Dossier → 🎧 Hear "Echoes in the Wire" (Ryan & Cassidy) ↗
Pioneer of The Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™ • Composer of "Escape Velocity (Ad Astra)"

Cassidy O'Connell

Co-Lead Vocals, Analog Synthesizers, Grand Piano & Chief Audio Architect

The sonic architect of The Stardust Engine. Operating from the center of her 360-degree circular analog synthesizer rig ('The Engine Room'), Cassidy engineered the zero-gravity Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™ and composed the 15-minute two-disc magnum opus 'Escape Velocity (Ad Astra)' after escaping Apex Records' coerced pop formulas.

📄 Full Archival Dossier → 🎧 Explore The Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™ Playlist ↗
Architect of the 1992 Friction Walkout & 1994 Apex Settlement

Holly O'Connell, J.D., CFA

Band Manager, Legal Architect & Co-Driver (Class A CDL w/ Passenger & Airbrake)

Ryan and Cassidy's fiercely protective younger sister. When Apex executive Julian Vance attempted to coerce Ryan and Cassidy during the October 14, 1992 'Friction' sessions, Holly pulled the plug, led the 1994 legal victory that reclaimed 100% of the band's master tapes, and earned her Class A CDL alongside Evan and Tyler so no outside driver could ever endanger her family again.

📄 Full Archival Dossier → 🎧 Stream "Forger Nation: The War Chest (1997)" ↗
Identical Twin Maternal Cousin • Joined at CPI in 1986

Evan Wright

Bass Guitar, Fretless Bass, Moog Taurus Pedals & Co-Driver (Class A CDL)

Joining Ryan and Cassidy at CPI in 1986 alongside his identical twin brother Tyler, Evan's driving basslines and sub-orbital Moog Taurus pedal sustains form the gravitational floor of The Stardust Engine. Holds a Class A Commercial Driver's License with Passenger and Airbrake endorsements.

📄 Full Archival Dossier → 🎧 Stream "Midnight Drivers (2001)" ↗
Identical Twin Maternal Cousin • Joined at CPI in 1986

Tyler Wright

Acoustic & Electronic Drums, Percussion & Lead Fleet Driver (Class A CDL)

Evan's identical twin brother and the rhythmic propellant ('Engine') behind every stadium anthem. After the 1990 I-81 crash, Tyler earned his Class A CDL with Passenger and Airbrake endorsements to personally command the wheel of the 2002 Sainte-Claire 45H3 ('The Iron Horse') and the 2004 Prairie Coachworks RLFD30.

📄 Full Archival Dossier → 🎧 Stream "Progress Street (2004)" ↗

The Stardust Engine (ERR-001)

Named after the very first song Ryan, Cassidy, Evan, and Tyler wrote together at CPI in 1986—celebrating their shared love of the cosmos (“Stardust”) and the rockets to get you there (“Engine”).
